brewing.notes: A common starting point for herbal infusions: boiling water, about five minutes.

description:
A sweetened Caribbean drink made from the bark or fruit of Colubrina trees, usually spiced, often with aniseed. It goes by mauby in the English-speaking islands, mavi in the Spanish-speaking ones and mabi in the French-speaking ones.

Brew it as you would other herbal infusions. If the plant is new to you, check that it is safe for you first, especially when pregnant or on medication.
history: It began as a home-fermented drink made in small batches and is now mostly a commercial, unfermented soft drink, often sold as a syrup to dilute, though home and street versions persist. In Puerto Rico the fermented, foaming style is called mavi champán. It can have a laxative effect on first-time drinkers.
processing: Dried plant material, as with most herbal infusions.
harvest_season: Depends on the plant and the place.
appearance_liquor: Depends on the plant; usually pale to amber.
taste_profile: Sweet at first, somewhat like root beer or sarsaparilla, turning into a long bitter finish without astringency.
vintage_note: Herbal infusions are not sold by vintage: buy recent stock and use it within a year or so.
